opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research grants max £20,000; Research and Travel grants max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months) for most categories; individuals (sculpture historians, academics, conservators) only for the Research and Travel category. Not for individuals developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections (acquisition, conservation, cataloguing, display); Conferences, Lectures and Publications (up to £5,000); Long-Term Research grants (multi-year, e.g. permanent collection catalogues); Research and Travel grants (for sculpture historians, academics, conservators). Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round (closing 1 September 2026) is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture; artist fellowships for visual arts practitioners (research only, no studio facilities).
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation and travel/subsistence expenses. Includes Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships and Senior Fellowships (six weeks). Applications closed for 2026/27; next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA and MA dissertations; plus Henry Moore Institute publications to £50 value, library deposit and abstract publication

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines; dissertation submitted within the past academic year at a UK university; must relate directly to sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes awarded for outstanding extended writing (dissertations) on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn 2026.
